props.description: The text style from the theme's type scale. Defaults to `body`.
props.name: type

props.description: The text to show; it may hold inline elements and nested Text.
props.name: children

props.description: The colour of the text: `muted` for secondary copy, a status tone for meaning. Defaults to `default`.
props.name: tone

props.description: The horizontal alignment; `start` and `end` follow the text direction, `justify` is iOS-only on native. Defaults to `start`.
props.name: align

props.description: True to cut the text to one line with an ellipsis; assistive technology still reads all of it.
props.name: isTruncated

props.description: The BCP 47 language of this text when it differs from the screen's, for example `ar` inside an English page.
props.name: lang

props.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
props.name: ref

props.description:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.
props.name: render
